name: Videha Mithila–Vajji–Anga qualified historical boundary layers

metadata.warning: These polygons are schematic research envelopes derived from published descriptions/maps. They are not cadastral, legal, surveyed, or exact ancient frontiers. Boundary uncertainty is part of the data model.
metadata.licenseNote: The Vajji and Anga derivatives retain CC BY-SA 3.0 attribution to Avantiputra7/Wikimedia Commons. The Mithila envelope is a new schematic interpretation of the published textual/map description cited in its feature metadata.

properties.name: Mithila historical-cultural frame (Karan 1984)
properties.temporalScope: Not a single-period polity. Used only as a cultural-historical geographic frame.

historicalGeometryEvidence.sourceCitation: Pradyumna P. Karan, ‘Landscape, Religion and Folk Art in Mithila: An Indian Cultural Region,’ Journal of Cultural Geography 5(1) (1984), pp. 85–101; esp. pp. 87–88 and Fig. 1, ‘Mithila Culture Region’.
historicalGeometryEvidence.geometryScope: Schematic envelope for the Mithila cultural region using the published north/Himalayan-foothill, south/Ganges, west/Gandak and east/Kosi framing together with Fig. 1; not a political frontier.
historicalGeometryEvidence.method: Low-resolution manual geographic envelope from the source’s explicit river/foothill description and published map; simplified for web research orientation.
historicalGeometryEvidence.derivativeNotice: New Videha research-envelope geometry; coordinates are intentionally simplified and must not be read as a surveyed or timeless boundary.

properties.name: Vajji approximate polity envelope, c. 500 BCE

historicalGeometryEvidence.sourceCitation: Avantiputra7, ‘Mahajanapadas (c. 500 BCE),’ Wikimedia Commons; map states that realm boundaries are approximate and cites H. C. Raychaudhuri, Irfan & Faiz Habib (1995), J. E. Schwartzberg (1992), Upinder Singh (2009), and related scholarship.
historicalGeometryEvidence.geometryScope: Approximate Vajji polity envelope for c. 500 BCE, digitized schematically from a published historical map whose own documentation describes the boundaries as approximate.
historicalGeometryEvidence.method: Low-resolution manual polygon derivative for research visualization; simplified rather than treated as a surveyed historical frontier.
historicalGeometryEvidence.derivativeNotice: Adapted/simplified by Videha from the cited CC BY-SA 3.0 historical map; changes were made and the geometry remains approximate.
